items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Bartok wrote them, and they struggle over Bartok.

ctx.x: Did you ever have occasion where you had a string section come in or mostly classical players and was there an attitude problem at all?

Sometimes. I’ll tell you, strangely the attitude problem — I hate to say this — is with the string teachers. It’s not with the young people that are learning. They want to come in and play the stuff. The teachers say well it’s not too valuable, you know you have to learn your sonatas and this and that and whatever. And I find it’s unfortunate. When I was at Eastman, Ray Wright began a program up there with a studio orchestra which was never there and it’s still a great orchestra. He’s not with us anymore. But he…
Well let me take you back a few years. You were born in the Dominican Republic. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
